title: Mark Zuckerberg’s creative plan to pay California’s proposed billionaire tax without losing control of Meta
slides: Can Zuckerberg pay California's billionaire tax and keep Meta?
The proposed tax targets unrealized gains, not just income
He found a creative workaround most billionaires overlook
Founders in high-tax states may soon face the same choice
Ask your accountant about control-preserving strategies now
thread_text:
1. The tax hit he dodged

Zuckerberg's tax bill on unrealized Meta gains would be massive, but he found a way to keep control without selling shares.

2. Not a wealth tax

California's proposal targets paper gains, forcing billionaires to pay on unsold stock. Most assume it means selling.

3. The overlooked move

He used a strategy that lets him pay the tax without dumping shares: borrowing against his stake.

4. Founders in the crosshairs

If you built a company in a high-tax state, this same dilemma could land on your desk soon.

5. Your move

Ask your accountant about control-preserving strategies before the tax man combs your gains. Does your plan survive?

instagram.caption:
California’s proposed billionaire tax would force Zuckerberg to pay on unsold Meta stock—most assume that means selling shares and losing control.

The tax targets unrealized gains, not income, so founders could owe millions on paper wealth without cash on hand.

His workaround: borrowing against his stake to pay the bill without dumping shares.

If you built a company in a high-tax state, this same choice may land on your desk sooner than you think. 💼
